requirements.text: Stuff the paper into the cup.
requirements.source_phrase: Stuffing the paper into the cup

outcomes.description: Paper is stuffed into the cup.
outcomes.target: The paper is visibly placed inside the cup, with evidence that it has been stuffed into it rather than merely resting nearby or on its rim.
outcomes.reference: The requested edit is stated in the instruction: “Stuffing the paper into the cup”.

nodes.question: Is the paper visibly inside the cup, with evidence it has been stuffed into it rather than merely resting nearby or on the rim?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image shows the paper placed inside the cup and visibly stuffed into it. Fail if the paper is only nearby or on the rim, or the image shows no progress toward placing it inside. Unknown if the image does not provide enough evidence to determine whether it is inside and stuffed.
nodes.binding: Assess only the requested paper-in-cup edit, using the image evidence; unrelated edits do not count as progress.

nodes.question: Comparing the source and edited images, does the edited scene show the source white paper and blue cup (allowing changes in appearance or orientation), and what visible evidence indicates whether the paper has moved toward or into the cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass only when the edited objects can be identified as the source paper and cup and visible placement shows progress toward putting the paper into the cup, even if it is not yet stuffed inside. Fail when the objects are identifiable but the paper remains in its source position or otherwise shows no movement toward the cup. Unknown when object identity, visibility, or placement is too ambiguous to determine progress. Do not infer no progress merely because completion is not shown.
nodes.binding: Use the source image to anchor the white sheet and blue cup; allow their appearance and orientation to change in the edit. Assess only continuity of these objects and visible progress toward placing the paper into the cup; proximity alone is not progress.

nodes.question: Does the image provide enough evidence to determine whether the paper has been stuffed into the cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image clearly resolves whether the paper is inside the cup and stuffed into it. Fail if the image clearly shows it is not stuffed into the cup. Unknown if visibility or ambiguity prevents a determination; retain this as unresolved rather than inferring completion or absence.
nodes.binding: Use only visible evidence of the paper’s placement relative to the cup; do not treat proximity or contact with the rim alone as proof of stuffing.

nodes.question: Does the image show the paper stuffed inside the cup?
nodes.criteria: Use s1 for evidence of the requested stuffed-inside placement, s3 for source-object continuity and progress, and s2 only for whether placement is resolvable. Complete only with clear evidence the source paper is stuffed inside the source cup. Partial only when s3 establishes progress but s1 does not establish completion. Absent only when s3 establishes no progress. If identity, progress, or necessary placement evidence is unresolved, report unknown; do not treat uncertainty or failure to see completion as absence.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

response.content: {"accepted":false,"reason":"The support checks do not provide independent, sufficient evidence for the requested relation and extent. s1 combines completion with a coarse placement judgment, while s2 merely asks whether that same completion is resolvable and is nested under s3, which checks progress rather than resolution. The fulfillment rule then treats s1 failing to establish completion as enough for partial when s3 shows progress, without requiring s2 to establish that the paper is not stuffed; this can label an unresolved completion partial. The checks also do not clearly establish that the cup is the source cup, as s3 anchors both objects but its pass criterion only requires identifying the source paper and cup. The composition therefore permits unsupported partial outcomes and lacks reliable evidence for the full requested relation."}

parsed.reason: The support checks do not provide independent, sufficient evidence for the requested relation and extent. s1 combines completion with a coarse placement judgment, while s2 merely asks whether that same completion is resolvable and is nested under s3, which checks progress rather than resolution. The fulfillment rule then treats s1 failing to establish completion as enough for partial when s3 shows progress, without requiring s2 to establish that the paper is not stuffed; this can label an unresolved completion partial. The checks also do not clearly establish that the cup is the source cup, as s3 anchors both objects but its pass criterion only requires identifying the source paper and cup. The composition therefore permits unsupported partial outcomes and lacks reliable evidence for the full requested relation.
